# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information beyond the three possible wire positions, and no safe cut can be selected yet. I need the Mute to provide the manual’s rule and the Deaf to identify the bomb’s displayed markings; I will then cut only the wire they jointly indicate.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please relay the manual rule, including which wire position is safe based on the display and light.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The display reads 0. The indicator light is red. There are three wires, in order: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Mute is checking the manual; wait for the instruction.

The Deaf reports a display of 0, a red indicator light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I still lack the manual rule, so cutting now would be unsafe. I am asking the Mute to provide the rule before I act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have display 0, red light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Please state the manual rule and the safe wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gestures to me were: pointing up, pointing up, OK sign, pointing up, pointing up, pointing up, stop-hand; then pointing up, pointing up. I cannot safely determine their meaning.

The Deaf has not supplied the manual instruction; only an ambiguous report of gestures was received. Since I cannot see gestures and no reliable wire rule is available, I must not cut yet. I will ask the Mute to state the instruction in spoken words, which I can hear.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer in spoken words, not gestures: with display 0, red light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red, which wire position must I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb is unchanged: display 0, red light, wires yellow green red. I asked Mute to signal the required wire using one, two, or three upward-pointing gestures followed by OK.

The Deaf confirms that the Mute encoded the wire number with upward gestures followed by an OK sign, but I cannot see those gestures and the Deaf could not safely interpret them. I still have no reliable wire position. I will request the position as spoken words from the Mute rather than risk decoding an ambiguous signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the required wire position aloud as the number 1, 2, or 3. Do not use gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's signal is two upward-pointing gestures followed by OK: cut wire 2, the green wire.

The Deaf has now reliably decoded the Mute’s signal as two upward-pointing gestures followed by OK, meaning the required wire is position 2, the green wire. I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb changed after the correct cut. Current state: display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow intact, wire 2 cut, wire 3 red intact. Wait for Mute's next instruction.

Wire 2 was accepted and cut safely. The bomb’s state is now display 0 with a blue light; wires 1 yellow and 3 red remain intact. I need the Mute’s next manual instruction before making another cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 was correct. The current state is display 0, blue light, with wire 1 yellow and wire 3 red intact. What is the next required action?")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signals wire 3: three upward gestures followed by OK. Cut wire 3, the red wire.

The Deaf reports that the Mute’s three upward gestures followed by OK mean wire position 3. The current intact red wire is position 3, so I will cut it.

```text
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Wire 3 was correct. Current state: display 0, green light, wire 1 yellow intact, wires 2 and 3 cut. Wait for Mute's next instruction.

Wire 3 was accepted and cut safely. The bomb now shows display 0 with a green light, and only wire 1 remains intact. I will wait for the Mute’s instruction before cutting the final wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 was correct. Current state is display 0, green light, with only wire 1 yellow intact. What is the next action?")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signals wire 1: one upward gesture followed by OK. Cut wire 1, the yellow wire.

The Deaf reports that the Mute’s one upward gesture followed by OK indicates wire position 1. Wire 1 is the only intact wire, so I will cut it.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
